model.name: Digital Signature / Proof
model.purpose: Attach, to any signed or sealed subject, the durable context that lets an agent understand what was signed, by whom, under which method, when this can be proven, and on what evidence a verification verdict rests and can be independently replayed later.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-034 is a mixin that carries signature and proof context for a subject owned by another model. It covers the proof object and its binding to signed data; the signer or sealer as bound by the credential; the signing method, algorithm and container profile; trusted time as evidence distinct from signer-claimed time; verification evidence sufficient for independent replay; and the durability of that evidence over decades. It is format-neutral: ASN.1, XML, JSON, PDF containers, Git objects, MCP resources and database rows are projections. It does not operate certification authorities, time-stamping authorities, transparency logs, archives or audit systems, and it does not evaluate, enforce or decide; it records what an accepted external application produced and what a later party needs in order to reach the same result.
in_scope: The proof object itself: immutable bytes, format and profile, placement relative to the signed data, and the digest binding it to that data.
The signer or sealer as bound by the proof: credential, certificate or key identifier asserted, and the subject attributes a relying party must be shown.
The signing method: signature and digest algorithms and parameters, canonicalization and transforms, claimed signature policy or commitment, container profile and level.
Trusted time as evidence: time-stamp request imprint, token identity, authority and policy reference, nonce, accuracy, and the ordered relation to signature generation and to each validation.

Verification evidence sufficient for independent replay: signature input digest, certification-path and revocation snapshot with freshness, trust configuration, algorithm policy, verifier identification, validation instant, verdict and reasons.

Durability of evidence: embedded versus external evidence packaging, renewal by new time-stamps or evidence records, algorithm and key expiry, evidence-chain continuity, optional corroboration references, and recorded anomalies and supersessions.
out_of_scope: Operation of certification authorities, time-stamping authorities, trusted lists and transparency logs, including issuance, supervision, merge delay and status publication.
Signature creation, signing-key generation and custody, and attestation of a signature-creation device or of sole control.
Signer authentication and authorisation, and the business meaning or legal effect of the signed transaction.
Execution of retention, legal hold and destruction, and the audit trail of access to these records.
Archive storage mechanics, blockchain anchoring services, notarial services, and case or evidence management workflows.
The runtime signature-validation application itself: its internal algorithms, decision engine and enforcement behaviour.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Certification authority, trusted list and trust-service supervision
boundary_notes.distinction: This model carries authority identifiers, certificate references, policy pointers and a trusted-list state digest as parameters of one validation. Issuance, supervision, qualification lifecycle and status publication remain with the trust-service registry; reproducing those records here would create a divergent second master copy.

The model records the token, its imprint binding, accuracy and policy reference as evidence. Clock synchronisation, UTC traceability, time-stamping unit key management and TSA audit are the authority's own operations and are referenced, never restated as local facts.

Inclusion and consistency proof references and signed checkpoints are optional corroboration of publication. Log operation, merge delay, gossip, monitoring and the log's own audit semantics belong to the log model; a log entry never establishes signer identity or the truth of the signed content.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Records retention, legal hold and archive storage
boundary_notes.distinction: This model asserts immutability and a minimum-evidence floor and defines a tombstone shape. Deciding and executing retention, hold and destruction, and operating archive storage, belong to the adopting Dimension's retention and archive models.
Everything from key generation to the moment a signature value exists is out of scope; the model begins at the produced proof object and its bindings.

Access events, break-glass reads and rejected writes are emitted to the Dimension's audit or logging model. This model does not define audit-record structure, audit retention, audit immutability or any evaluation over audit trails.

sources.title: Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Time-Stamp Protocol (TSP)
sources.relevance: Normative structure of TimeStampReq (messageImprint, reqPolicy, nonce, certReq) and TSTInfo (policy, serialNumber, genTime, accuracy, ordering, nonce, tsa), including the rule that ordering is only strict when accuracy intervals do not overlap.

sources.title: ESSCertIDv2 Update for RFC 3161
sources.relevance: Requires a TSA certificate identifier (ESSCertID or ESSCertIDv2) as a signerInfo attribute and mandates SigningCertificateV2 for any hash algorithm other than SHA-1; grounds algorithm agility in token-to-key binding.

sources.title: Evidence Record Syntax (ERS)
sources.relevance: EvidenceRecord, ArchiveTimeStamp, ArchiveTimeStampChain and ArchiveTimeStampSequence; reduced hash trees; time-stamp renewal versus hash-tree renewal; and the recommendation for redundant evidence records under different algorithms and authorities.

sources.title: Extensible Markup Language Evidence Record Syntax (XMLERS)
sources.relevance: XML projection of evidence records with an explicit CanonicalizationMethod per chain, CryptographicInformationList for certificates and revocation data, and the same two renewal strategies; demonstrates container independence of the evidence semantics.

sources.title: X.509 Internet Public Key Infrastructure Online Certificate Status Protocol - OCSP
sources.relevance: Defines producedAt, thisUpdate, nextUpdate, revocationTime and revocationReason, the nonce binding, and the acknowledged replay exposure of pre-produced responses; the basis for revocation freshness evidence.

sources.title: Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Certificate and Certificate Revocation List (CRL) Profile
sources.relevance: Section 6 path validation inputs (prospective path, current date/time, trust anchor information, initial policy set and constraint flags) and CRL thisUpdate/nextUpdate; establishes that a verdict is meaningless without its validation time and trust anchors.

sources.title: CMS Advanced Electronic Signatures (CAdES)
sources.relevance: Signature forms BES/EPES/T/C/X/A, validation-data attributes, grace period, arbitration model, and the explicit distinction that signing-time is a signer claim while a time-stamp token is proof of existence.

sources.title: Certificate Transparency Version 2.0
sources.relevance: Merkle tree, signed tree head/checkpoint, inclusion and consistency proofs, log identity and maximum merge delay, and the security position that logs enable detection of misissuance but do not themselves prove legitimacy.

sources.title: ETSI EN 319 102-1 Electronic Signatures and Infrastructures (ESI); Procedures for Creation and Validation of AdES Digital Signatures; Part 1: Creation and Validation
sources.relevance: Validation model: signature validation application, validation constraints, proof of existence, validation time and best-signature-time, the status indications TOTAL-PASSED / TOTAL-FAILED / INDETERMINATE with sub-indications, and validation of basic, time-stamped and long-term signatures.

sources.title: ETSI TS 119 102-2 Electronic Signatures and Infrastructures (ESI); Procedures for Creation and Validation of AdES Digital Signatures; Part 2: Signature Validation Report
sources.relevance: Interchange structure for a validation report: validation objects, proof-of-existence entries, signer information, validation constraints evaluation, status with indication and sub-indication, and a signature over the report itself.

sources.title: DSS Documentation - Digital Signature Service (eSignature building block)
sources.organization: European Commission, Directorate-General for Digital Services
sources.relevance: Reference implementation of EN 319 102-1: enumerated sub-indications, baseline levels B-B/B-T/B-LT/B-LTA, content/signature/archive time-stamp roles as proof of existence, past signature validation when a certificate is revoked after signing, revocation-freshness and cryptographic-sunset constraints, and trusted-list driven trust anchors.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-102, Recommendation for Digital Signature Timeliness
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Independent authority for the claimed-time versus trusted-time distinction, the role and verification requirements of a Trusted Timestamp Authority, and the use of contemporaneous tokens to preserve signatures across later key compromise.

sources.title: XML Signature Syntax and Processing Version 1.1
sources.relevance: Reference/Transforms/DigestMethod/DigestValue model, two-step reference then signature validation, and the explicit rationale that canonicalization is what makes a digest input reproducible across implementations.

sources.title: ETSI EN 319 142-1 Electronic Signatures and Infrastructures (ESI); PAdES digital signatures; Part 1: Building blocks and PAdES baseline signatures
sources.relevance: Container-specific projection of long-term evidence in PDF: Document Security Store for validation material, document time-stamps for archival, and the advice against relying on the VRI dictionary because DSS entries already reference the same material.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 (eIDAS), Articles 32, 34 and 42
sources.organization: European Union (text as published on legislation.gov.uk, The National Archives)
sources.version_or_date: Regulation of 23 July 2014; retained-EU-law text accessed 2026-09-04
sources.relevance: Article 32 requires the validation system to give the relying party the correct result and to let it detect security-relevant issues; Article 34 requires preservation to extend trustworthiness beyond the technological validity period; Article 42 requires time binding that precludes undetectable change and an accurate time source linked to UTC.

bundles.name: Trusted time as evidence
bundles.description: Independently issued temporal evidence for a signature or proof: what was submitted for time-stamping, what the returned token asserts, which authority and policy stand behind it, and how the resulting instants may and may not be ordered against signer-claimed time.
bundles.rationale: A signature alone cannot say when it was made. RFC 5126 and NIST SP 800-102 separate a signer-claimed signing-time from a proof of existence, and eIDAS Article 42 requires binding of date and time to data so that undetectable change is precluded, with an accurate source linked to UTC. Trusted time therefore has to be its own bundle rather than an attribute of the signature.

layers.name: Time-stamp request and token evidence
layers.description: The imprint that binds a token to a specific object, and the immutable token that fixes an instant with a serial number, accuracy bounds and a policy claim.

findings.name: Time-stamp request and message-imprint binding
findings.description: The hash algorithm and imprint value submitted for time-stamping, the requested policy, the nonce and certificate-request flag, and above all an unambiguous statement of which object the imprint covers: the signature value, the signed data, or a prior evidence element. Without this statement a token proves the existence of an unknown digest.

artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system identifier is the issuing authority identifier plus the token serial number. Generation time is never an identifier.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The authority, its certificate chain, its published policy and its supervision status are issued, versioned and withdrawn by trust-service and supervision registries that this model does not operate. Materialising them as local artefacts would create a second master copy that silently drifts from the register of record and would invite an agent to treat a stale local copy as authoritative. What this finding legitimately holds is purely inline reference data: identifiers, resolvable pointers with versions, the observed status and its observation instant, and the binding of that authority to one specific token.

findings.description: The defensible ordering among signer-claimed signing time, each proof of existence, revocation and compromise instants, and each validation instant, together with the accuracy and clock-uncertainty bounds that make some pairs unorderable.

data_elements.name: Claimed signing time
data_elements.description: Signer-asserted signing instant, retained as an unproven claim and never promoted to a proof of existence.

data_elements.name: Best signature time
data_elements.description: Earliest instant at which the signature is proven to have existed, derived from the recorded proof set.

data_elements.name: Proof-of-existence entry
data_elements.description: One derived assertion that a named object existed at or before a given instant, with the evidence element that supports it.

data_elements.name: Ordering assertion
data_elements.description: A pairwise assertion that one recorded instant precedes another, qualified by the bounds that permit or forbid the assertion.

data_elements.name: Clock uncertainty interval
data_elements.description: Bound within which a recorded instant may deviate, from stated accuracy or from a documented clock-quality assumption.

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: Instant at which this model observed or ingested the evidence, always recorded separately from the asserted event time.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are derived relational assertions computed over proof artefacts that are already declared elsewhere in the model; they carry no bytes of their own. Freezing them into an artefact would fossilise a derivation that legitimately changes whenever a further proof of existence, a revocation record or a compromise determination arrives, and a frozen ordering table would be easy to mistake for independent evidence. Keeping them inline forces every ordering claim to be recomputed from the retained proofs, which is exactly the property an independent replayer needs.

bundles.name: Replayable validation evidence
bundles.description: Everything a party who was not present at validation needs in order to reach the same conclusion: what the signature covered, which certificates and revocation data were used and how fresh they were, which trust anchors and algorithm constraints applied, which tool produced the verdict, at which instant, and with what indication and reasons.
bundles.rationale: eIDAS Article 32(2) requires the validating system to give the relying party the correct result and to let it detect security-relevant issues; RFC 5280 makes the validation date/time and trust anchors explicit inputs to path validation; and ETSI EN 319 102-1 with TS 119 102-2 turns the outcome into an indication, a sub-indication and the set of validation objects each conclusion depended on. A verdict without those inputs is not evidence.

layers.name: Validation inputs and configuration snapshot

findings.inline_only_rationale: Verifier identity, version and configuration are descriptive parameters of a verdict that is already declared as an immutable artefact in the sibling finding, and the replay contract is a statement about which of the model's existing artefacts must be retained together. Minting a further artefact here would duplicate the validation report's payload and create two descriptions of a single immutable event that could drift apart. Keeping this finding inline makes the replay contract a property of the evidence set rather than another object competing to be the record of truth.

bundles.name: Evidence durability, corroboration and degradation

bundles.rationale: RFC 4998 and RFC 6283 define renewal by new time-stamps or by hash-tree rebuild precisely because algorithms and keys expire; eIDAS Article 34 requires preservation that extends trustworthiness beyond the technological validity period; and RFC 9162 makes clear that a transparency log detects misissuance but does not establish legitimacy. Durability, corroboration and degradation therefore need explicit structure and explicit limits.

composition.purpose: Signature and proof evidence is a subordinate part of the enclosing cryptographic-attestation context registered as the parent. Standards treat validation data as belonging to the electronic signature rather than standing alone, so this model nests rather than competes; the parent supplies the enclosing subject and its own identity and lifecycle.

composition.target: Subject entity models carrying signed artefacts (documents, credentials, records, messages) in the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: As a mixin this model attaches proof and validation evidence to any signed subject without redefining that subject's identity, classification or lifecycle. The subject model remains the system of record for the object; this model records only what proves and validates the signature over it.

composition.target: Trust-service registry model covering certification and time-stamping authorities, trusted lists and supervision status
composition.purpose: Carry authority identifiers, certificate references, policy pointers, a trusted-list state digest and the observed qualification status as parameters of a specific validation. Issuance, supervision, status publication and authority lifecycle stay with the target; this model must not reproduce or re-derive them.

composition.target: Transparency-log model covering append-only log operation, checkpoints and monitoring
composition.purpose: Carry log identity, entry locator and proof references as optional corroboration of publication, with a mandatory negative scope statement. Log operation, merge delay, gossip, monitoring and the log's own audit semantics remain with the target.

composition.target: Signed content and document model of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Bind evidence to the signed data object by version-pinned reference plus digest, so that replay can proceed on digests alone when content is detached or unavailable. The content model owns that object's versioning, storage and lifecycle.

composition.target: Retention, disposition and legal-hold model of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Deletion, hold and disposition over proof bytes and validation records are decided and executed under the target model. This model contributes only the immutability constraint, the minimum-evidence retention floor and the tombstone shape, and never asserts that a disposition was lawfully executed.

composition.target: ETSI EN 319 102-1 and ETSI TS 119 102-2 signature validation and validation-report model
composition.purpose: Align indications, sub-indications, validation objects, validation time and proof-of-existence semantics so that verdict records interchange cleanly. This is an alignment for interoperability, not a conformance claim; no clause-level conformance is asserted here.

composition.target: IETF evidence record syntax family (RFC 4998 and RFC 6283)
composition.purpose: Align renewal kinds, chain and sequence continuity and redundant-chain semantics with archive time-stamp structures, while keeping the model independent of any single container so that embedded and detached evidence are treated alike.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names one accountable owner and one deputy for signature-evidence records; ownership of the signing key, the certificate, the authority and the signed content stays with their own owners and is never absorbed here.

The owning package publishes a versioned registry of accepted validation applications and accepted time authorities, and every verdict and every trusted-time record cites the registry entry that authorised its producer.
The owning package declares a minimum evidence set and a replay contract; a record below that floor is marked incomplete or non-replayable rather than being reported as valid.
The owning package registers a retention floor, a renewal calendar and an escalation path for evidence that cannot be renewed before its protecting algorithm weakens.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one namespace per adopting Dimension in the form `<dimension>/signature-evidence/`, with sub-namespaces for proofs, validation records, evidence packages and assertions. External identifiers keep their issuing namespace verbatim: policy object identifiers, issuer plus certificate serial number, authority plus token serial number, log identifiers and report identifiers are never re-minted locally, and any local surrogate is stored beside the external identifier, never in place of it.
registry_links: Trusted-list or trust-store registry used to resolve trust anchors and observe authority qualification status
Algorithm policy registry recording acceptable suites, minimum parameters and sunset instants
Local registry of accepted validation applications and accepted time authorities with versions
Replay-contract registry declaring, per subject class, which inputs must be retained together

canonicalization_rules: Proof bytes are canonical exactly as received: never re-encode, re-wrap, re-indent or normalise a token, certificate, revocation response, signature or evidence record; store the received octets and derive any presentation form separately.

Where a digest is computed over structured data, record the canonicalization and transform algorithm identifiers and their parameters alongside the digest; a digest without its transform chain is not replayable and must be flagged as such.

Times are stored in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z, converted at ingestion from GeneralizedTime, UTCTime or any source form, with the original lexical value retained verbatim next to the normalised value.
Identifiers are compared by issuing namespace plus value, never by display string; certificate and token identity is issuer plus serial number, not subject name or file name.
Codes from external vocabularies, including sub-indication values, are stored verbatim; local mappings are recorded as annotations and never replace the source value.
patch_rules: Proof bytes, recorded digests, verdicts, validation instants and renewal records are append-only; a correction is a new supersession or invalidation assertion that names the affected records and leaves them byte-identical.

Additive patches may attach new evidence — a later time-stamp, a fresher revocation response, a renewal record, an additional digest under a new algorithm, a corroboration reference — but may never remove, reorder or rewrite an earlier element.

Descriptive metadata that is not itself evidence, such as labels, cross-references and local classifications, may be patched in place provided the prior value and the actor are retained as provenance.
A patch that would make a retained verdict non-replayable must set the replayability flag and record the reason in the same operation.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional evidence element, a new corroboration reference or an additional digest is backward compatible; narrowing a cardinality, removing an evidence element, or changing the meaning of a digest, indication or renewal kind is breaking.
Indication and sub-indication vocabularies extend by addition only; an unknown value is preserved verbatim and treated as indeterminate, never silently dropped or coerced to a known value.

A projection change between ASN.1, XML, JSON, a PDF container, Git objects, a document store or an interface surface must leave evidence identity, digests and proof bytes unchanged; if a projection cannot carry an element, the export declares the shortfall rather than omitting it silently.
Algorithm migration is additive: new digests are recorded beside historical ones, and no compatibility break may be used as grounds to discard a historical digest.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the system of record that issued or holds the artefact: issuing authority identifier plus time-stamp token serial number, certificate issuer plus serial number, responder identifier plus production instant for a status response, or the validating application's own report identifier.

Governed global identifier or IRI where no master-system identifier exists: a registered policy object identifier, a governed transparency-log identifier, or a registered namespace IRI for an evidence package.

UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only where neither of the above exists, and always stored together with the digest of the artefact it names and with the identifier of the covered object.

A date, a generation time, a validation instant, a version label or a file name is never an identifier. Digests disambiguate but do not identify across algorithm migration, so an artefact identified only by digest carries every historical digest recorded for it.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Every recorded instant uses RFC 3339 with seconds precision and an explicit numeric offset or Z; sub-second precision is retained whenever the source supplies it and the original lexical form is kept verbatim. Event time asserted by an external party — signature generation, token generation time, revocation time, response production, this-update and next-update, checkpoint time, renewal time — is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time, meaning the instant at which this model received, captured, re-checked or replayed the evidence, and both are stored whenever they differ. Accuracy or uncertainty bounds are recorded alongside any instant that carries them, and no strict ordering is asserted between two instants whose bounds overlap.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Artefacts belonging to an issuer-ordered series — time-stamp tokens, archive time-stamp chain entries, validation reports for one signature, supersession assertions — retain the issuer's own sequence value and are named `<issuer-namespace>:<series>:<sequence>`. A local counter is never substituted for an issuer sequence; where no issuer sequence exists, a local monotonic sequence is used and labelled as local. Gaps in a series are recorded explicitly as gaps and are never closed by renumbering or backfilling.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artefact is stored with at least one digest under a currently acceptable algorithm plus every historical digest previously recorded for it, so that algorithm migration never erases an earlier binding. Digests are re-verified on read of proof bytes and on a scheduled cycle. An artefact whose recomputed digest matches no recorded digest is quarantined as a broken record, reported through the gap-reporting function, and never silently replaced, repaired or re-fetched over the original.

policies: Trusted time counts as evidence only when independently issued; a signer-asserted signing time is retained as a claim and is never promoted to a proof of existence, however plausible it looks.

A validation verdict is a dated observation, not a permanent property of a signature. Every verdict is stored with its validation instant, constraint snapshot and verifier identification, and a later contradictory verdict is a new record that never overwrites an earlier one.

A transparency-log entry, inclusion proof or checkpoint corroborates publication only. It never establishes signer identity, authorisation, or the truth or lawfulness of the signed content, and the negative scope statement travels with the reference.
Completeness is asserted only against a declared replay contract. Where evidence is insufficient, the record is indeterminate — neither valid nor invalid — and the specific shortfall is named.

This model records and reports; it does not evaluate, enforce or dispose. Evaluation belongs to the external validation application, enforcement to the adopting Dimension's policy machinery, disposition to its retention model, and audit trails to its audit model.

read: Reading proof bytes returns them byte-identically as stored, together with every digest recorded for them and the result of the integrity re-check.

Reading a verdict must return its validation instant, its constraint snapshot reference and its verifier identification; returning an indication alone is a reporting defect and must be rejected by the interface.
Superseded records remain readable and are always returned together with the assertions that superseded them; hiding a superseded record is prohibited.
Reads distinguish evidence gaps from negative findings, so an agent is never able to read a missing dependency as a failed signature.
create: Creation records the artefact bytes, its source, its ingestion instant and at least one digest in a single atomic step; a partial ingestion is rolled back rather than left as a fragment.

A trusted-time record is admitted only with its imprint binding recorded, including the hash algorithm and an unambiguous identification of what was hashed, and only if any request nonce is echoed identically.

A verdict record is created only with references to the validation material set and constraint snapshot that produced it and with the producing application resolved in the accepted-validator registry.
Creation never mints a local identifier where a master-system or governed identifier is available.
update: Proof bytes, recorded digests, verdicts, validation instants, renewal records and prior assertions are immutable after creation.

Permitted updates are strictly additive: further digests under new algorithms, further renewal records, further corroboration references, further supersession assertions, and corrections to non-evidential descriptive metadata with prior values retained.
Reinterpretation of an earlier record is expressed only as a new assertion naming that record; in-place reinterpretation is prohibited.
An attempted mutation of immutable content is rejected and emitted as a rejected-write event to the adopting Dimension's logging arrangements; this model neither defines nor owns that log.
delete: This model destroys nothing of its own accord. Evidence is retained for at least the longest of the declared replay-contract retention floor, the next renewal deadline, and any active hold; while any of those is in force, disposition rights are suspended for every role including the owner.

Where disposition is authorised, the record is tombstoned rather than erased: identifiers, all recorded digests, the issuing-authority and covered-object references, the creation instant, the disposition instant and the authorising decision reference are retained, while proof bytes and payload are removed.

Deleting an element on which a retained verdict depends requires that verdict to be flagged non-replayable in the same operation, with the missing dependency named; silent partial deletion is prohibited.

Execution of deletion, legal hold and disposition is owned by the adopting Dimension's retention, disposition and legal-hold model named in the composition ledger, which also owns the lawfulness determination. This model contributes only the immutability constraint, the minimum-evidence floor and the tombstone shape, and never asserts that a deletion was lawfully executed or that a hold was correctly released.

roles.name: Signature-evidence owner
responsibilities: Accountable for the completeness and integrity of the evidence set for a defined subject class
Approves the replay contract, the minimum evidence set and the retention floor
Refers disposition and hold questions to the retention model rather than deciding them locally

roles.name: Evidence custodian
responsibilities: Ingests proof bytes and validation material atomically with digests and both time classes
Maintains digest coverage across algorithm migration and runs scheduled integrity re-checks
Quarantines and reports broken records without repairing or re-fetching over the original

roles.name: Validation operator
responsibilities: Runs validation only through applications listed in the accepted-validator registry
Records verdicts with validation instant, constraint snapshot and verifier identification
Records unrecognised sub-indications verbatim and never coerces them to known values

roles.name: Preservation engineer
responsibilities: Maintains the renewal calendar against algorithm and key expiry and executes renewals in time
Chooses between time-stamp renewal and hash-tree rebuild and records which was used and why
Establishes redundant evidence chains where a single chain would be a single point of failure

roles.name: Independent replayer
responsibilities: Re-runs validation from the exported replay package without access to the originating system
Records any divergence as a new verdict and, where warranted, raises a supersession assertion
Reports which replay steps still depended on network retrieval; audit records themselves remain with the Dimension's audit model

access.default_rule: Evidence is readable by roles with a declared need to verify or preserve it; write access is limited to append-only creation by the evidence custodian, validation operator and preservation engineer; and no role, including the owner, holds mutate or destroy rights over proof bytes, digests or recorded verdicts.
exceptions: Signed content and certificate subject data may carry personal data. Where the adopting Dimension restricts it, digests, references, indications and verdicts remain visible while the content payload is withheld, so verification remains possible without disclosure.
A pseudonymous certificate is flagged to the relying party rather than resolved; resolving a pseudonym is an authority decision outside this model and outside any role defined here.
Under an active legal hold, disposition and tombstoning rights are suspended for all roles until the hold is released by the retention model.
Break-glass read of a withheld payload requires a named authorising decision reference recorded with the access before the payload is released.

Export of a replay package to an external party may be restricted where the constraint snapshot or trust-store state is itself confidential; in that case the export carries digests and pointers instead of the confidential body and declares the substitution.
audit_requirements: Every read of a withheld payload, every break-glass access, every rejected mutation attempt, every export of a replay package and every supersession assertion is emitted with actor, authorisation reference, affected record identifiers and observation instant.

These events are emitted to the adopting Dimension's audit or logging model, which owns audit-record structure, retention, immutability and any evaluation over the trail; this model neither stores nor interprets audit trails and makes no claim that an audit trail is complete.

required_fields: Accepted validators and time authorities registry URL
Retention, hold and disposition policy URL
read_order: AGENTS.md first, to resolve the model identity, its type as a mixin and the five location fields
Specification URL, for the boundary, bundles, findings, data elements and the concepts this model explicitly does not own
Storage type URL, for the chosen projection and the immutability and append-only guarantees the store actually provides
Interface URL, for the read and append operations, the export surface and the rule that a verdict is never returned without its validation instant, constraint snapshot and verifier identification
Processes URL, for ingestion, trusted-time recording, verdict recording, renewal, corroboration and supersession procedures
Algorithm policy URL and the accepted validators and time authorities registry, before recording any new trusted-time record or verdict
Replay contract URL and the retention, hold and disposition policy, before exporting evidence or proposing any disposition

coverage.claim: This structure covers the durable evidence surface of WM-XCT-034 — trusted time distinct from signer-claimed time, replayable validation evidence, long-term preservation, optional corroboration and evidence degradation — grounded in IETF time-stamping, evidence-record, OCSP, path-validation, CAdES and transparency specifications, in the ETSI validation and validation-report model as implemented by the European Commission's reference service, in NIST guidance on signature timeliness, in W3C canonicalization semantics and in eIDAS validation, preservation and time-stamp requirements. It is not a completeness claim: signature creation, key custody, sole-control attestation and non-PKI proof systems are deliberately outside what is asserted here, and every structural node is traceable to a cited source rather than to convention.

checklist.notes: Identity priority puts the authoritative master-system identifier first (authority plus token serial, issuer plus certificate serial, responder plus production instant, report identifier), then a governed IRI, then a locally minted UUID or ULID. Dates, generation times and file names are explicitly rejected as identifiers, and digests are treated as disambiguators that must be carried in full history across algorithm migration.

The lifecycle modelled is that of the evidence, not of the signature or of any external authority: ingestion, renewal deadlines, chain continuity, supersession and tombstoning. Authority qualification lifecycle and certificate lifecycle are referenced to the trust-service registry rather than modelled locally.

Verdict-to-dependency references, imprint-to-covered-object bindings, package-to-signature bindings, redundant chains and assertion chaining are all explicit, each carrying a digest so the relationship survives the loss of one endpoint.

Generation time, accuracy, ordering flag, revocation and production instants, validation instant, report production time, renewal instants and observation times are separated. Ordering is refused where accuracy intervals overlap, and best-signature-time is derived rather than asserted.

Every element records its source, its acquisition instant and whether it is held by value or by reference with digest; authority and list state are pointers with version and digest, never local copies.

Owner and deputy are named for evidence records only; key, certificate, authority, content, retention and audit ownership are all pushed to their own models through composition links and boundary notes.

Verdict, sub-indication, per-constraint results, dependency references, verifier identification and the replay contract are modelled as recorded evidence of an external evaluation. The model records outcomes and reports gaps; it never evaluates or enforces.

Default read-for-need with append-only write and no mutate or destroy rights; exceptions cover personal data in signed content, pseudonym flagging without resolution, holds, break-glass and confidential constraint snapshots. Audit events are emitted, not owned.

A retention floor derived from replay contract, renewal deadline and active holds; tombstoning that keeps identifiers, digests and references while removing payload; mandatory non-replayable flagging when a dependency is deleted; and explicit assignment of execution and lawfulness to the adopting Dimension's retention model.

Aligned to the ETSI validation-report structure and to the IETF evidence-record family as alignments rather than conformance claims, with verbatim preservation of external codes, projection-invariance rules for digests and proof bytes, and declared shortfalls where a target format cannot carry an element.
Treated as a first-class bundle with its own imprint binding, token identity, authority reference and ordering discipline, keeping signer-claimed time permanently demoted to a claim.
Algorithm policy with sunset instants, additive digest history, both renewal kinds, redundant chains, and an explicit collision-migration question with a residual-risk statement.
A named replay contract distinguishes invariant from variable inputs, flags network-dependent steps, and requires divergence to be recorded as a new verdict rather than an edit.

Unavailable and retracted responders, expired certificates, revocation and compromise after proof, compromised authorities, orphaned content, clock uncertainty, missed renewals and log failure each have a question and an anomaly class.
Digests, accuracy bounds, uncertainty intervals, freshness ages and tree sizes are the quantities the model carries; all are recorded with the algorithm or unit that produced them.

Geographic location has no bearing on the durability of signature evidence. Jurisdiction affects which trust framework and retention rules apply, and that is carried as a reference to an external policy rather than as a spatial attribute of the evidence.

known_omissions: ETSI deliverables were cited from their published deliverable URLs, whose served PDFs were not machine-readable through the research tooling at access time. Their clause-level detail here is corroborated through the European Commission's DSS reference documentation and through the IETF specifications rather than quoted directly, so ETSI-derived structure should be re-verified against the deliverable text before any conformance claim.
Signature creation, signing-key generation and custody, signature-creation-device attestation and signer authentication are deliberately absent from this structure.
Remote and server-side signing, including evidence of sole control over a remotely held key, is not modelled; it would need its own findings and probably its own model.

Non-PKI proof systems — zero-knowledge proofs, threshold and multi-party signatures, post-quantum hybrid schemes and blockchain anchoring — are acknowledged as possible proof carriers but no structure is claimed for them.
Preservation-service protocol operations, meaning the request and response surface of an external preservation service, are referenced but not modelled.

Time-mark based proof of existence, permitted by CAdES, appears only as a classification value and has no dedicated finding; systems relying on provider-held audit records for proof of existence will need more structure than this provides.
Countersignature, multi-signature and signature-ordering evidence within one container is only partly reachable through the ordering finding and would benefit from explicit treatment.
conflicts: RFC 3161 makes the ordering field optional and false by default, so two tokens from one authority are strictly orderable only when their accuracy intervals do not overlap. Implementations that treat generation time as a total order will disagree with a conformant reading; this model follows the conformant reading and refuses the assertion.

RFC 6960 permits pre-produced OCSP responses and acknowledges the resulting replay exposure. A freshness rule expressed purely as next-update can therefore accept a response produced before a revocation, so the model records nonce presence and the caveat rather than treating next-update as sufficient.

RFC 4998 recommends redundant evidence records under different algorithms and different authorities, whereas common container practice maintains a single archive time-stamp chain. A single chain is widespread practice, not a normative sufficiency claim, and the model records the single-point-of-failure note instead of endorsing it.

ETSI EN 319 142-1 advises against relying on the PDF VRI dictionary because the same material is already referenced from the document security store, yet widely deployed tooling still writes VRI entries. Both may be present and may disagree, so the packaging finding requires an explicit reconciliation rule.

eIDAS Article 32 expresses validation obligations in legal terms tied to qualified signatures, while EN 319 102-1 expresses outcomes as indications and sub-indications. A passing indication is a technical result and is not by itself a legal determination; the model keeps them as separate recorded facts.

NIST algorithm-transition practice and European algorithm-suite practice do not always deprecate the same parameters at the same time, so the constraint snapshot must record which policy applied rather than assume a single global schedule.
regional_assumptions: The eIDAS articles were read from the retained-EU-law text published by legislation.gov.uk. The quoted wording of Articles 32, 34 and 42 matches the EU original in the parts relied on, but the retained version omits paragraphs; the EUR-Lex text governs in EU contexts and should be used for any binding interpretation.

Trusted-list mechanics assume a supervision-list arrangement of the European kind. Other jurisdictions govern trust stores differently, so the model carries a versioned pointer and state digest rather than assuming any particular list.

NIST guidance on signature timeliness and algorithm transitions is United States federal policy; adopting Dimensions elsewhere must bind their own algorithm policy and cannot inherit these schedules by default.
Nothing here presumes any particular legal effect for a signature in any jurisdiction, nor that a qualified status in one framework transfers to another.
adversarial_checks: Does any node claim ownership of a neighbour's operational semantics? Verdict recording is defined as recording an external application's output with explicit no-evaluation wording; the time-authority finding is deliberately inline-reference-only; corroboration is pointer-based; audit events are emitted, not stored. Each is restated in boundary notes and in the composition ledger.

Could a transparency-log inclusion proof be read as proof of signer identity? A dedicated definitional question, a mandatory scope-statement data element carried with every reference, and a standing policy all make the negative explicit, matching the RFC 9162 position that logs enable detection of misissuance rather than establish legitimacy.

Can a verdict or a proof be silently changed or removed? Update rules forbid mutation, correction is by supersession assertion, deletion is tombstone-only with mandatory non-replayable flagging, and rejected mutations are emitted as events. An agent following the interface rules cannot produce a clean-looking history.

Would evidence still be interpretable after the digest algorithm protecting it is broken? The integrity rule keeps digest history additive, both renewal kinds are modelled, redundant chains are asked about, and the collision-migration question forces a residual-risk statement covering the pre-migration interval.

Is a date ever load-bearing as an identifier? Identity priority rejects generation times, validation instants and file names, and the serial naming rule forbids substituting a local counter for an issuer sequence or closing a gap by renumbering.

Can an evidence gap be misread as a negative finding? Read rules require gaps and negative findings to be distinguished, the gap-reporting function separates them explicitly, and the completeness policy forces an indeterminate result rather than a valid or invalid one where evidence is short.

Does the model quietly duplicate the trust-service registry? The only trust-service data held locally are identifiers, versioned pointers, a state digest and an observed status with its observation instant — enough to reproduce one validation, not enough to act as a second register.
